## Active

### D-168 — Timer assertions carry slack because Node fires timers early

> _2026-09-15 · core/blong-chain · active_

A step that awaits `setTimeout(resolve, 50)` completes in 49.x ms about once in 60 runs, because
Node's timers can fire marginally before their nominal delay: measured over 400 iterations,
`duration` was 49 in seven of them. Asserting `duration >= 50` was therefore a real flake rather
than a slow machine. The assertions in `core/blong-chain`'s tests now subtract `TIMER_SLACK_MS` of 5
ms from the nominal delay and print the observed value.

### D-255 — The marker is snapshot and a bare [] is a sync barrier, with no alias

> _2026-09-23 · core/blong-chain · active_

The chain marker is `snapshot` (`ILib.snapshot`, `SnapshotMarker`), a bare `[]` is a **sync
barrier**, and `checkpoint` now means only the progress point a handler reports. No deprecated
alias: an alias is a second name for one thing, which is how the word came to carry three meanings
in the first place. Eleven call sites were `lib: {group, checkpoint}` destructures, and
`snapshot-context.test.ts`'s test titles are golden snapshot keys, so retitling that file needed the
matching keys renamed in the `.cjs`.

### D-265 — A step boundary read compares content, not a count

> _2026-09-25 · core/blong-chain · active_

A step own progress is read as the difference between the invocation list at two boundaries, and a
difference alone is not enough: the documented way a scenario scopes its assertions is to reset the
list (meta.progress = []) before its own call, which can leave exactly as many entries as the
previous step did - and every step of demo/handler-test-poc does exactly that. A step that spreads
the list back with additions is appending by another name. So the read asks whether the list still
begins (entry for entry, by object identity) with what it held: if it does, the tail is this step
own entries; if it does not, the list was replaced and all of it belongs to this step. Identity
rather than equality, because the entries are the objects the recorder pushed.

### D-272 — A point is a comment, a branch is a sub-test

> _2026-09-26 · core/blong-chain · active_

A checkpoints list is rendered as two different things now, because the two shapes are not the same
kind of thing. A branch is a sub-test: the points taken inside it belong together, and a report that
does not group them is not showing what the code did. A point is a comment: it is a moment a step
passed through rather than a piece of work, so it does not earn a test of its own — but its data is
what a reader looks for, so it is printed beside it.

The data is capped rather than printed whole: the five shortest properties, values longer than forty
characters left out, and the count of what was left out said, so a short line never reads as the
whole story and an object of ten fields cannot crowd out the three numbers beside it.
`IProgressNode` had to carry `data` for this, since the tree was built without it.

What this changed for anyone counting: a scenario's test count drops, because the points it
announced are no longer tests. That is the point of the change, and it is why the demo went from 51
to 24.

Allure is untouched by this and still writes every point as a step, which is where the room for the
full data is. The two reports therefore agree on the shape (branch as group, point inside it) while
differing in how much of a point they print.
